answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on scarce, non-transferable trust paths rather than cheap identity claims. Each agent must be vouched for by independent sponsors who hold stake at risk; joining a river of transactions, the newcomer enters a trellis where every edge carries collateral. Forging a thousand identities then means finding a thousand genuinely independent backers, each losing a deposit if the puppet misbehaves. Reputation at the zenith cannot be conjured, only earned across settled sessions, so a swarm of fresh keys starts at zero and pays real fees to climb.
